length.text: Small: usually under 30 cm; record about 49 cm

overview.text: De Kay's Brown Snake is a small, harmless snake of eastern North America and Central America. It is very common and is often found in towns, gardens and city parks.

identification.text: Brown to grey with a paler stripe down the middle of the back, edged with small black spots. The belly is pale brown or pinkish with tiny black dots at the edges.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually less than 30 cm (12 in) long; the record is about 49 cm. Newborns are only about 7.7 cm long.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Southern Ontario and Quebec, most of the eastern half of the United States, and south through Mexico to Guatemala and Honduras.

habitat.text: Most kinds of wet and dry habitats east of the Great Plains, from sea level to about 1,400 m. It likes moist places and is most often found near people - in cities more than in the countryside.

reproduction.text: Mates in spring after its winter rest and gives birth to live young. Females can store sperm, so the babies are born when food is plentiful.

recognise.text: Small brown snake with a pale stripe down the back.
Two rows of small black spots along the stripe.
